keyPoints: ["Fusion combines light nuclei into a heavier nucleus","Three proton–proton cycle steps","Mass defect becomes energy","E=mc² and stellar temperature/pressure conditions"]
modelAnswer: Nuclear fusion is the combination of two light nuclei to form a heavier nucleus. In the proton–proton cycle, (1) two protons form deuterium with emission of a beta particle and energy, (2) a proton combines with deuterium to form helium-3 with energy emitted, and (3) two helium-3 nuclei fuse to form helium-4, emitting two protons and energy. The products have less mass than the starting nuclei; this mass defect is converted to energy according to E=mc² (about 26.3 MeV per cycle). The high temperature and pressure in stars provide the conditions needed to overcome electrostatic repulsion and initiate fusion.
